TS.PROJECTS-CHESS-GAME-SHORT-DESCRIPTION: Challenge your friends in a chess game.
TS.PROJECTS-CHESS-GAME-DESCRIPTION: Designed as part of a university project, this chess game allows two players to compete on a 2D board. The game offers the ability to change tile colors as the player wishes, restart a game, view possible moves for a selected piece, and see previously played moves.
TS.PROJECTS-MATRIX-SHORT-DESCRIPTION: Console application for solving matrices using various methods.
TS.PROJECTS-MATRIX-DESCRIPTION: Designed as part of a university project, this console application allows solving matrices using various methods such as the Gauss method, Gauss-Jordan method, Cramer’s method, Jacobi method, and the inverse matrix method.
TS.PROJECTS-SERIALIZE-SHORT-DESCRIPTION: Console application for serializing and deserializing objects via a JSON file.
TS.PROJECTS-SERIALIZE-DESCRIPTION: This console application allows serializing and deserializing objects from a JSON file, provided the object has an appropriate constructor, offering a simple and flexible solution for data management.
TS.PROJECTS-NICOLET-SHORT-DESCRIPTION: The city of Nicolet tasked me with providing a way to predict all socio-environmental aspects related to their city.
TS.PROJECTS-NICOLET-DESCRIPTION: Designed as part of an internship, this project aims to predict the socio-environmental aspects of the city of Nicolet using machine learning algorithms such as linear regression and neural networks. The data used comes from various sources, including weather data, city data, and environmental data. The results are generated as charts, including a socio-environmental doughnut chart, a vertical or horizontal bar chart, a line chart, or a pie chart.
TS.PROJECTS-BEAUDOIN-SHORT-DESCRIPTION: Creation of a conversational agent specialized in writing press releases.
TS.PROJECTS-BEAUDOIN-DESCRIPTION: During my internship at Beaudoin Public Relations, I created a press release drafting agent that used both the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and the Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE) as prompting methods. The application scanned the computer for a specific directory. Once found, it identified the files whose names contained one or more keywords, then kept a reference to them in order to use them during its training.
TS.PROJECTS-MASTERS-SHORT-DESCRIPTION: Design of an LLM-based agent integrating ethical, environmental, and digital sovereignty principles.
TS.PROJECTS-MASTERS-DESCRIPTION: Development of a generic and modular agent capable of instantiating various specialized agents based on fundamental principles such as ethics, digital sovereignty, and environmental challenges. This agent may, for example, propose strategies to reduce a country’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, explore the Web to identify relevant funding sources, or conduct technological monitoring to detect emerging innovations. All decisions and recommendations will be guided by local, cultural, and ethical values.
TS.PROJECTS-WINDOWS-BMR: Automated extraction of doors and windows from architectural plans
TS.PROJECTS-WINDOWS-BMR-SHORT-DESCRIPTION: The project involved developing a tool to automate the extraction of doors and windows from architectural plans. A multimodal AI system combining computer vision, OCR, and language models analyzed the plans, matched openings with their schedules, and structured the extracted data.
TS.PROJECTS-WINDOWS-BMR-DESCRIPTION: This project was completed during my employment at BMR. It aimed to develop an automated solution capable of analyzing complex architectural drawings and extracting all relevant information about doors and windows. My role involved designing the system architecture, developing the tool in Python, and optimizing the workflow to process buildings containing more than 500 openings. The application identified each door and window, then extracted its tag, dimensions, quantity, location, floor, façade, assigned room, and number of insulated glass units. It also compared floor plans, elevations, and specification schedules to associate each opening with the correct information. Validation and deduplication mechanisms were implemented to reduce errors, identify missing data, and prevent the same opening from being counted multiple times. The results could then be visually reviewed and exported to CSV or Excel. The solution relied on multimodal artificial intelligence combining computer vision, optical character recognition (OCR), and language models. This combination enabled the system to understand architectural drawings, interpret technical annotations, and automatically organize the extracted information into structured data.
